Precision has always appealed to me because laboratory work turns careful testing into results that matter far beyond the bench. What draws me most to a Laboratory Technician role is the way accurate, methodical work supports wider scientific and healthcare goals, whether in research, quality processes, or patient outcomes. Originally from Bangladesh, I hold a Master’s degree from a university ranked in the global top 100, and through my studies and professional experience I have completed 3 projects with tangible outcomes. That combination of advanced study and practical delivery confirmed for me that reliable data depends on consistency at every stage, from sample preparation to documentation. One of my favourite family memories captures this connection perfectly: after hearing my stories from a busy week in the lab, my younger sibling began turning our kitchen into a “mini lab,” carefully labelling cups of juice like test samples, which made me realise how clearly my enthusiasm for methodical work and discovery came across at home as well as at work.

A key part of my development has come through steady learning in practice. Over more than a year, I worked regularly with a new laboratory tool and subject area that was unfamiliar at first, building confidence step by step until using it became part of my normal workflow. In one team setting, a recurring issue was slowing sample processing, so I introduced a simple workaround that reorganised how materials were prepared and checked before testing, reducing repeated delays for the group. Colleagues and supervisors now regularly come to me with difficult questions, including queries outside my immediate area, and I am often the person asked to help trace a result back through the process when something does not look right. During a long assignment with several setbacks, including repeated revisions and unexpected delays, I kept the work moving over an extended period and put in extra time when needed to bring it through to completion. I am now keen to continue developing as a Laboratory Technician, bringing careful accuracy under pressure, dependable follow-through, and a genuine commitment to producing meaningful results the wider team can trust.

Before breakfast on a family holiday, I once showed a relative recovering from a minor injury a few simple mobility exercises, only for everyone else to join in and turn it into an impromptu stretching session. That memory has stayed with me because it captured what first drew me to physiotherapy: a genuine interest in how the body heals and adapts, and the satisfaction of helping people regain confidence in their movement and daily lives. Originally from Peru, I chose this path because it brings together science, empathy, and practical problem-solving in a way that creates visible, meaningful progress. Through my Bachelor’s degree at a university not listed in the major global rankings, I deepened that interest and built the foundations I now want to apply in a Physiotherapist role.

Through my studies, I became especially interested in how clinical assessment can be turned into rehabilitation plans that feel realistic and encouraging for each individual. In particular, one completed project with a tangible outcome required me to follow a patient-focused piece of work through to its final result; when parts of the process took longer than expected, I continued refining the work over an extended period and gave additional time where needed so that it could be completed properly. Over more than a year of steady practice, I also became comfortable using a new clinical tool and subject area that had initially been unfamiliar, moving step by step from basic use to applying it more confidently in routine work.

Beyond this, my practical experience has shown me the importance of sound procedures and teamwork in physiotherapy. In day-to-day cases, I work through established assessment and treatment steps carefully, and when an unusual situation arises, I seek guidance so that the patient receives the right approach. I also work well alongside colleagues, and when someone asks how I completed a task or used a technique, I am happy to talk them through it. Overall, I am ready to bring my background, my Bachelor’s degree, and my commitment to personalised rehabilitation into a Physiotherapist position where I can support steady recovery, independence, and long-term wellbeing.

Few environments shape a person’s experience as completely as a well-run hotel, and that has long been what draws me to hospitality. I have always been inspired by the way a hotel can turn an ordinary trip into a lasting memory, and that interest grew into a wider appreciation of how thoughtful service, careful coordination, and attention to detail create a welcoming atmosphere for every guest. This is why I want to build my career as a Hotel Manager: I am motivated by the chance to bring hospitality, leadership, and service together in a setting where guests feel at ease and teams can work smoothly behind the scenes. I hold a Master’s degree from a university not listed in the major global rankings, and that academic experience strengthened my commitment to structured learning and practical results. During one extended assignment, I stayed with the work through delays and revisions, returning to it over a long period and putting in extra time when needed until it was completed. I have also completed 1 project with a tangible outcome, which reinforced my interest in work that leads to visible improvements.

Over time, I became comfortable with a new tool gradually through more than a year of regular use, moving from basic tasks to using it confidently in day-to-day work. When a recurring issue was repeatedly slowing my team down, I introduced a practical workaround that reduced the disruption and helped work continue more smoothly. In shared work settings, colleagues have often come to me with questions, and I make time to talk them through the steps I use so they can apply them in their own tasks. That combination of guest awareness and steady coordination is central to the kind of Hotel Manager I want to be, creating a calm, polished environment where high standards are maintained consistently. Originally from the Netherlands, I also value the personal side of hospitality: during a family stay at a sister property, my relatives began spotting small service touches they recognised from stories I had shared, turning the visit into a light-hearted “hotel manager’s eye” challenge. That moment reminded me how meaningful thoughtful hospitality can be, and I am eager to bring my background, experience, and long-term commitment to a hotel where I can continue learning and contribute to memorable guest experiences.

The work took sustained effort over a long period, including revising drafts after feedback and staying late when deadlines and clinical duties overlapped. Through these experiences, I have strengthened my communication, teamwork, organisation, adaptability, and attention to safe practice. Overall, I am eager to bring this foundation to a Registered Nurse role and contribute dependable, compassionate care every day.
